business_scope.primary_industry_name: Expatriate Worker Cross-Border Money Transmission Service

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 2011)
Colombia–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 2007) and Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2014)
Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Colombia, Mexico, Peru, Chile)
OECD Instruments (Colombia acceded to the OECD Convention effective 28 April 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (SAS regime), Articles 1, 2, 4, 5 and 17; Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971), Articles 98, 110, 111 and 130; Law 526 of 1999 (creation of UIAF) as amended; Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT offences and obligations) as amended; Law 1955 of 2019 (National Development Plan), Articles 119 and 120, establishing the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB); Decreto 830 of 2021 implementing the RUB; DIAN Resolution 000075 of 2021 and subsequent amending resolutions (mandatory UBO filing regime); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular Básica Jurídica (consolidated by Circular Externa 025 of 2021), Chapter on SARLAFT and PEP identification; FATF Recommendations as adopted into Colombian law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the foreign incorporator's passport or national identity document (UBO evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial or Consular authority of the country of origin; Colombian Consulate where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention on Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation, in force for Colombia since 2001); Consular Legalization for non-Apostille member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or commercial registry authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, in the absence of Apostille coverage, full Consular Legalization at the Colombian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Power of Attorney granted by the UBO or incorporator for execution of the SAS by-laws and local representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin, subsequently legalized or apostilled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (signatory state) or Consular Legalization (non-Apostille state); notarial Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of funds declaration and bank reference letter of the UBO (AML/CFT provenance evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or designated financial institution of the UBO; notarized and sworn before a Colombian notary where necessary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consular-legalized; accepted as notarized certified copy with sworn affidavit where banking secrecy restricts direct disclosure

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized representatives against the UIAF consolidated risk lists, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and OFAC sanctions programs, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Lista de Activos Bloqueados and Listas Vinculadas maintained by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia; enhanced due diligence (EDD) thresholds apply to all domestic and foreign PEPs under the SFC Circular Básica Jurídica (Circular Externa 025 of 2021), including family members and close associates of Colombian public officials; any entity entering the remittance industry must integrate FATF Recommendations 10 and 25 into its SARLAFT framework prior to licensing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rues.org.co, operated through the local Cámara de Comercio (for this mandate, Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá at www.ccb.org.co) under the supervisory oversight of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be set in Latin script and transliterated into Spanish when originating from a foreign language; the name must end with the token 'S.A.S.' or the full phrase 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' as the lawful suffix; registration is refused where the requested name is identical or materially similar (homonimia) to an existing entry in the RUES database, or where it creates confusion with a reserved or previously incorporated name; names containing untransliterable characters are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens 'Banco', 'Bank', 'Banca', 'Bancolombia' — require prior Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) authorization and a special statutory license
Tokens 'Financiera', 'Financiero', 'Crédito' as activity descriptors — sensitive financial-sector terms requiring SFC name consent and a regulated activity license
Tokens 'Seguro', 'Aseguradora', 'Reaseguradora' — require SFC authorization under the insurance regime
Tokens 'Fondo', 'Fiduciaria', 'Custodio' — reserved for licensed collective investment or fiduciary institutions
Tokens implying public or governmental character: 'Nacional', 'Estatal', 'Ministerio', 'Superintendencia', 'Presidencial' — prohibited for private companies absent an express ministerial permit
Token 'Colombia' used as a standalone name element — requires special SIC and Chamber authorization and a descriptive complement

Generic or misleading tokens for the remittance business: 'Remesa Nacional' without an SFC license, 'Central', 'Monetario', 'Offshore', 'Trust' — subject to rejection under Article 65 of the Colombian Commercial Code
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cámara de Comercio rejects the proposed name, the incorporator may (i) file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Chamber within ten (10) business days of notification; (ii) alternatively or subsequently file a 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within ten (10) business days; proceedings are governed by Ley 1437 of 2011 (Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo), Articles 74, 75 and 76; if administrative remedies are exhausted without success, the incorporator may file a judicial action before the competent Tribunal Administrativo within four (4) months of the final administrative decision, and may request precautionary measures extending the name reservation until a judicial ruling is issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or registered-agent-only address is not permissible as the operational seat for a money transmission undertaking. At the pre-incorporation stage, a representative registered address is accepted as the statutory domicile of the SAS under Law 1258 of 2008, but the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia will require a physical operational branch in Colombia — with staff, accounting records, IT systems and an AML/CFT function at a locatable premise — prior to activation of the remittance license; third-party virtual office arrangements may only serve as an interim administrative placeholder for the pre-license phase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High Likelihood — approximately 75% probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia or UIAF within the first twelve (12) months of licensed operations; SFC routinely conducts pre-authorization on-site verification visits for remittance agents, and the likelihood increases where the entity processes local cash-pickup clearing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Decree 1074 of 2015 (Chamber fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the SAS private incorporation deed and legalization of corporate books
Registration of the incorporation deed and corporate documents with the Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Registro Mercantil
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory sliding-scale registration fee under the Colombian Commercial Code and Chamber tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) registration contribution (RUES component)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory contribution rate on mercantile registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign UBO documents (passport, good standing, power of attorney, source of funds declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and foreign competent authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-document apostille and consular tariff in the country of origin; approximate bundle cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS by-laws (estatutos), corporate governance charter and corporate minutes book framework
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SAS incorporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/SARLAFT compliance framework and remittance license gap assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for high-risk financial license preparation services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening database license (one-year pre-incorporation and launch phase)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for AML screening tools

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) UBO registration and filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (registration itself is free); compliance agent fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for UBO registration agency services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for one-year registered office service (first instalment)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Estatuto Legal de la Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 1, 5, 21-27; complemented by Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), arts. 98, 110, 114, 372; Ley 2069 de 2020 (Ley de Emprendimiento); for remittance licensing, Estatuto Orgánico del Sistema Financiero (Decreto 663 de 1993) and Circular Básica Jurídica C.E. 029 de 2014 of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES), under the technical supervision of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private Articles of Incorporation) submitted for mercantile inscription as 'Inscripción de Sociedad Comercial' in the Cámara de Comercio registry; a public deed (Escritura Pública) is required only if the founders opt for it or contribute real estate in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for SAS formation; the subscribed capital must be fully subscribed but payment may be deferred for up to two years (Ley 1258 de 2008, art. 5). Cross-border remittance licensing, however, requires the company to evidence a provisional technical capital/patrimonio técnico prescribed by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, which must be escrowed as a Certificado de Depósito a Término (CDT) or equivalent fiduciary deposit opened at a Colombian financial institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST ADMINISTRATIVE BOARD RESOLUTION No. 001 - [ENTITY NAME] S.A.S. UNDER Ley 1258 de 2008, at the sole-shareholder general meeting: 1. RESOLVED: share subscription and capital payment plan approved; founder subscribers hereby subscribe all authorized shares and payment installments are fixed in accordance with Article 5 of Ley 1258 de 2008. 2. RESOLVED: registered address adopted: Calle [address], Bogota D.C.; this domicile shall govern Camara de Comercio registration, DIAN NIT filing, and SFC licensing. 3. RESOLVED: appointments - [name] is elected Representante Legal (Manager) with unrestricted powers; [name] appointed Compliance Officer for the AML/FT regime. 4. RESOLVED: authorization - the Manager is empowered to execute all pre-incorporation and post-registration formalities, sign contracts with correspondent agents and banks, and file the remittance license before the SFC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Drafting of the Private Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Camara de Comercio de Bogota - RUES online window with notarial certification at a local Notaria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the homologation (certificado de homonimia) of the proposed corporate name via the RUES portal. Draft the Documento Privado de Constitucion in Spanish, specifying share classes, deferred payment terms, management structure and liquidation rules. Certify subscriber signatures before a notary or Chamber-authorized attesting officer; if contributors include real estate, protocolize the constitution as Escritura Publica.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate (homonimia)
Draft private Articles (Documento Privado de Constitucion)
Identity documents or passports of founding shareholders
Notarized power of attorney if executed through an agent
Acceptance letters for in-kind contributions and valuation statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, a new homologation request may be filed or the corporate name amended; adverse decisions by the Chamber may be appealed before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Inscription and Obtaining the Certificate of Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Camara de Comercio de Bogota - RUES physical service center or electronic inscription portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation dossier to the Chamber service window or RUES portal; pay registration tariffs calculated on the declared assets and the stamp tax (impuesto de timbre); register the company, its legal representative, subrepresentative, compliance officer and auditors in the mercantile registry; obtain the original 'Certificado de Existencia y Representacion Legal'.
required_dossiers: Notarized private Articles or certified copy of the public deed
Certificate of name approval (homonimia)
Signed acceptance of appointments of Manager, subrogated manager, compliance officer and statutory auditors as applicable
Preliminary RUT form for DIAN (with economic activity classification)
Evidence of payment of Chamber tariffs, stamp tax and registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Formal defects are corrected by a supplemental filing within the Chamber's prescribed cure period; rejection notices are subsanated by re-submission with an updated certificate of existence, with no loss of legal status between filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN - NIT and RUT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - electronic taxpayer services counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Unico Tributario (RUT) application electronically through the DIAN portal using the certificate of existence; complete the company legal information with economic activity code ISIC 6619 and the complementary remittance services code; select tax obligations for income tax (renta), complementary taxes, VAT if applicable, and district ICA; obtain the Numero de Identificacion Tributaria (NIT) resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation issued within 30 days
Identity document of the legal representative
Private Articles or public deed of incorporation
Registered office physical address and contact data
Electronic filing credentials of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the filing, respond with the required supplementary affidavit within the legal term through the DIAN electronic notice panel; adverse determinations may be appealed by recurso de reconsideracion within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Constitution of Capital Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Colombian commercial credit institution supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account in a supervised Colombian bank or financial cooperative; constitute the escrow term deposit (CDT) or fiduciary mechanism equal to the provisional technical capital required by SFC for remittance authorization; obtain the banker's certificate evidencing availability of funds, absence of liens, and the term of deposit.
required_dossiers: NIT and RUT certificates
Updated certificate of existence and legal representation (less than 30 days old)
First board resolution authorizing account opening and capital escrow
Identity documents of signatories and the compliance officer
AML-KYC source-of-funds affidavit of the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An undue refusal of account opening is remedied by filing a formal 'Derecho de Peticion' with the financial institution; if rejected without grounds, the company may approach an alternative supervised entity or report the conduct to the SFC consumer financial office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Cross-Border Remittance Operating License before the SFC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) - Directorate of Financial Institutions and Payments Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete license dossier through the SFC-specific processing window: constitutional and corporate governance documents, technical-financial business plan for SWIFT and local cash pickup clearing rails, AML/FT compliance program aligned with Circular Basica Juridica (SAGRILAFT), compliance officer appointment, IT and cybersecurity scheme, draft correspondent and paying-agent contracts, and the escrow capital certificate. Attend to any SFC technical requirement (requerimiento) and obtain the formal authorization resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
Articles of incorporation and mandatory corporate governance documents
AML/FT manual (SAGRILAFT) and SARLAFT implementation plan
Bank escrow capital certificate (CDT or fiduciary)
Three-year financial projections and business plan
Compliance officer appointment letter, resume and good-standing declaration
Shareholder and manager background and fit-and-proper statements
Model correspondents and paying-agent agreements, including cross-border clearing descriptions
IT security and operational continuity program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reply to the technical requirement within the statutory term; if the application is denied, file the recurso de reposicion before SFC within 10 days, and upon second instance an appeal (recurso de apelacion) to the Civil Court for Administrative Affairs; the corrected dossier may also be renewed with updated capital evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the UIAF as an Obligated Reporting Entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Unidad de Informacion y Analisis Financiero (UIAF) - Entity Registry and Transaction Reporting System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the UIAF system as an obligated entity under Law 1121 de 2006 and Law 190 de 1995; designate the compliance officer in the system; configure transaction alert modules for threshold reporting of cross-border remittances, cash pickup operations and SWIFT movements; obtain the UIAF registration certificate.
required_dossiers: SFC remittance license resolution
RUT and NIT certificates
AML/FT manual and compliance officer acceptance letter
Proof of implementation of the SARLAFT regime
Corporate powers of the signing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corrections of submitted data are done by immediate electronic rectification in the UIAF portal; if the registration is objected to, the company presents an explanatory brief and, if necessary, a request for reconsideration to the UIAF.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Operating Office, Physical Premise Clearances and License Annotation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Camara de Comercio de Bogota; Curaduria Urbana (local planning office); Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogota
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Annotate the SFC license and the authorized remittance activity in the RUES mercantile certificate; register the principal office and any service branches as 'establecimiento de comercio'; obtain the concept of land use compatibility (uso del suelo) from the Curaduria Urbana; obtain the fire safety certificate from the Fire Department and the occupational safety registration; finalize the pre-operational compliance dossier for the SFC post-license supervision team.
required_dossiers: SFC authorization resolution
Lease contract or ownership title for the registered office
Concepto de uso del suelo granted by the Curaduria Urbana
Certificado de Bomberos (fire-fighting and evacuation compliance)
Occupational health and safety program under Resolucion 0312 de 2019 registered with the ARL
Updated RUES certificate evidencing the license annotation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Department or Curaduria require adjustments, a site reinspection is scheduled after correcting physical deficiencies; where the Chamber refuses license annotation, the company may appeal to the SFC or SIC according to authority of the contested decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) - Delegatura para la Atencion de Intermediarios Financieros; physical premise clearances coordinated with Camara de Comercio de Bogota, Curaduria Urbana and Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorizacion de funcionamiento para la operacion de servicios de remesas transfronterizas (Cross-Border Money Transmission License) - Special Registry of Remittance Companies of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (EOSF, Decreto 663 de 1993; Circular Basica Juridica, C.E. 029 de 2014).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaria Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) de Bogota; national-scale consultations through the Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA); waste registration through the Corporacion Autonoma Regional (CAR) mechanisms.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV - Exempt from a Full EIA Report; the undertaking is an office/IT-based remittance technology service with no industrial manufacturing, so a simplified environmental registration (Registro de Generadores de Residuos Peligrosos) and municipal use authorization apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer network must comply with Resolucion 631 de 2015 parameter limits: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 under 400 mg/L, COD under 800 mg/L, TSS under 600 mg/L, and fats and oils under 40 mg/L, with discharge permit coordination with the municipal aqueduct company. VOC and combustion emission limits under Resolucion 909 de 2008 apply to any emergency diesel generator, requiring stack testing (particulate matter below 250 mg/m3). E-waste, batteries and fluorescent lamps must be surrendered to authorized reverse-logistics systems in accordance with Resolucion 1512 de 2010 and Decreto 4741 de 2005, with generator records kept for inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogota fire-safety certificate covering evacuation plan, fire extinguishers, smoke detection and emergency exits, renewable annually; structural load verification for office occupancy under Reglamento Colombiano de Construccion Sismo Resistente (NSR-10) with the responsible engineer's load certificate; occupational health and safety standards under Resolucion 0312 de 2019, registered with the Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL); land-use compatibility certificate issued by the Curaduria Urbana confirming the location is authorized for non-industrial office operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign legal entity must appoint a legal representative with domicile in Colombia and obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by completing the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) application through the DIAN portal or in-person at DIAN offices. The applicant must file the foreign company's certificate of incorporation, proof of the legal representative's appointment, a translated corporate resolution where applicable, and evidence of a local address. The NIT is irreversible and is the single tax identification number for income, VAT, and other fiscal obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election and no domestic hybrid mismatch election are available in Colombia. A SAS may, however, be admitted to the SIMPLE (Sistema Simple de Carga Tributaria) consolidated tax payment regime if its actual income, employee count, and activities satisfy the statutory thresholds, provided it is not carrying out activities expressly excluded by law. Taxpayers may also elect among certain ICA/IVA simplification rules only when the entity falls within the natural-person small trader classification; a SAS normally cannot use the 'no responsable' VAT status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for corporations. A SAS is required to register as a VAT responsible taxpayer if it performs any taxable transfers of tangible goods or taxable services in Colombia, even on an occasional basis. Natural-person small traders may be treated as 'no responsables' only when gross income in the preceding calendar year is less than 3,500 UVT and other statutory conditions are met, which is unavailable to corporate entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-responsible persons, including SAS entities, are required to use DIAN-authorized electronic invoicing. Invoices must be transmitted in near real-time to DIAN's web services through certified software using a digital signature. The invoice must include the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) code and a QR code, and must pass DIAN's real-time structural and tax verification before being delivered to the customer. Pilots, OEM software integrators, and cloud/API connection methods must comply with DIAN Technical Annex and Resolution 165/2023 onward.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated (excluded from IVA) when goods physically leave Colombia and title passes to a foreign buyer, or when services are provided from Colombia but are used exclusively outside Colombia by a recipient that is not domiciled in Colombia and that does not have a permanent establishment in Colombia. The exporter or service provider must obtain and preserve documentary evidence proving the foreign destination, actual use of the service abroad, and that the amount is invoiced to the foreign party. For remittance-related services, the commission or service revenue must be earned under an international service agreement and the underlying transactions must involve foreign payers or counterparties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration accepted and validated by DIAN (Declaración de Exportación), showing ISIC 6619 service classification where applicable
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign client, evidencing the 0% VAT status or express exclusion basis
Bill of lading, airway bill, or equivalent contractual transport evidence for goods, or for services: signed contract and service completion certificate
Foreign exchange declaration (declaración de cambio) documented in the Colombian forex market and the inward settlement certificate issued by the local bank or financial intermediary
Certificate of origin and any required authorizations when the transaction claims preferential tariff treatment or export incentives
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit export zero-rating claims retrospectively for up to the displacement tax assessment period. If a zero-rated export is disallowed because the service was not used abroad, the documentation is insufficient, the payment was not repatriated within the FX deadline, or the transaction is deemed artificial, DIAN assesses VAT at 19% on the gross value plus default interest and applies a substantial penalty of up to 200% of the omitted tax for fraudulent or materially inexact claims under the Colombian Tax Code. Criminal tax fraud charges may also be pursued under Law 2277 where there is intent to obtain an abusive VAT exemption or refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Republic of Colombia Central Bank), acting as the Foreign Exchange Authority under the Régimen de Cambios Internacionales; the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) supervises authorized FX intermediaries and the remittance operator license; the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF) receives AML/CTF reports; and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) enforces exchange-control penalties. Legal basis: Law 9 of 1991, the Banco de la República's Resolución Externa No. 1 of 2018, and Decreto Único Reglamentario 1068 de 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is fully convertible for current-account transactions when channeled through the official foreign exchange market ('mercado cambiario'). Capital-account inflows (equity subscriptions, loans, portfolio investment) may be freely converted but must be processed via an authorized local intermediary and formally registered with the Banco de la República to secure future capital repatriation, dividend remittance, and hedging rights. Profit (dividend) remittance is permitted without prior Central Bank authorization once the S.A.S. has satisfied its entity-level corporate income tax; the remittance is declared on the applicable Declaración de Cambio, and dividends destined to non-residents become subject to the corresponding dividend withholding tax regime, treaty-protected where applicable. There are no quota systems or dual exchange rates; the principal operational hurdle is documentary compliance at the moment of conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of goods and services are subject to mandatory 'canalización': 100% of export proceeds must be collected in Colombia through an authorized FX-market intermediary, deposited into a local bank account, and declared on the applicable Declaración de Cambio (Formulario No. 2 for goods; Formulario No. 1 for services and other concepts). For goods, the funds must be channeled into the Colombian financial system within a maximum of twelve (12) months from the date of shipment (embarque). For services, including cross-border remittance and BPO fee flows, the channeling term is the shorter period established in the underlying contract and accepted by the intermediary, commonly six (6) to twelve (12) months. There is no forced conversion ratio to COP if the exporter maintains a permitted foreign-currency deposit account with a local bank; however, the funds must always enter the national territory through the mercado cambiario before any use. Non-channeled export proceeds are subject to fines, exchange-control sanctions, and loss of hedging and tax benefits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (corporate current account with separate transit sub-account for foreign investment)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (corporate current account; treasury division handles Cambio declarations)
Operational Account (corporate current account); capital-escrow functionality conditional on credit approval
Operational Account (corporate current account) with foreign-currency settlement facility
Operational Account and USD-denominated clearing account (cuenta en moneda extranjera)
Operational Account (corporate current account); escrow arrangements not recommended

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal constraints. Foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) authorized in their home jurisdictions may not act as deposit-taking institutions, clearing members, or final settlement providers in Colombia without a local license. Under Law 1735 of 2014 and the SFC's SEDPE regime, any entity holding client funds, issuing electronic payments, or operating cash-in/cash-out networks in Colombia must be incorporated as a Colombian Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) or must use a licensed bank as custodian and settlement bank. For the S.A.S. remittance operator, foreign EMIs are viable only as limited technical rails: collection of foreign-origin funds, offshore FX conversion, and transmission of a settlement instruction to a local licensed payout partner. The EMI cannot serve as the sole liquidity clearing channel because final settlement must occur in COP through the SFC-supervised financial system with full beneficiary traceability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted in Colombia under Ley 2150 de 2021 and SFC fintech guidance, including video-KYC and electronic signatures. Nevertheless, for a High-Risk Special License segment (money transmission), Tier-1 Colombian banks generally require: (1) a physical meeting or equivalent live video interview with at least one legal representative holding registered powers (Certificado de Cámara de Comercio), (2) validation of the beneficial-owner register for any individual or entity holding more than 10% or otherwise exercising control, and (3) an on-site or virtual third-party inspection of the principal place of operations. Full remote opening is possible in principle, but the customary market standard for this business profile is a recorded compliance interview plus delivery of apostilled corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated S.A.S. with no operating track record, 100% foreign ownership, and a remittance/money-transmission bank relationship requested while the SFC special-license resolution is still pending.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certificate of incorporation and bylaws (acto constitutivo S.A.S.) including the beneficial-ownership annex; (ii) Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and current Cámara de Comercio certificate; (iii) minutes appointing the resident legal representative with limited and demonstrated powers; (iv) signed lease or service agreement for the local office; (v) business plan evidencing the remittance corridor and liquidity model; (vi) draft SARLAFT compliance structure with named compliance officer; (vii) apostilled constitutional documents and audited financial statements of the foreign shareholders; and (viii) tax-residence certificates of the ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consumer remittance agency with cash-pickup payouts, high transaction volumes in a single currency corridor, and a bank-perceived elevated money-laundering and terrorism-financing profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved AML/CFT manual under the SFC's Circular Básica Jurídica (SARLAFT framework) and Law 1121 of 2006; enhanced due diligence (EDD) policy for cash-pickup beneficiaries; geographic risk matrix; automated screening and transaction-monitoring procedures with threshold alerts; quarterly risk reports to the board; UIAF registration and suspicious transaction report (ROS) protocol; and a credible independent compliance audit plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual settlements from an offshore non-bank intermediary (e.g., an FCA-authorized EMI) in amounts inconsistent with the S.A.S.'s declared fee income and without a clear funds-flow trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full licensing documentation of the offshore counterparty; contractual evidence of the commercial relationship; funds-flow diagrams tracing each payment to the end beneficiary; detailed fee schedule and invoice reconciliation; sworn statement of corporate-source funds signed by the directors; and confirmation that the S.A.S. operates on an agency/escrow-only model with no client funds crossing its balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media hits on a significant shareholder or on a beneficiary country targeted by the local cash-pickup clearing network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated screening logs covering UN, OFAC, EU, and Colombian listings with date/time stamps; PEP identification and enhanced monitoring workflow; commercial justification for each corridor including volume caps; trade or origin documents for each counterparty; audit-trail files for false-positive resolution; and a legal opinion on economic-sanctions compliance for the destination jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign share capital of the S.A.S. must be wired via SWIFT MT103/202 to the account of an authorized Colombian FX-market intermediary. The remitter includes: beneficiary NIT (tax ID), full legal-entity name, and the purpose code 'Inversión extranjera directa en sociedad local' (Foreign Direct Investment). At the moment funds are credited, the bank files the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional (Formulario No. 5) with the Banco de la República, generating the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (Certificado de Inversión Internacional). This certificate is the legal precondition for future profit remittance, capital disposal/repatriation, and access to FX hedging instruments. If capital enters in USD or EUR, the intermediary converts it to COP on the FX market unless the S.A.S. holds an authorized foreign-currency account. The registration must be updated on any subsequent capital increase or decrease. The complete file must contain: the share-subscription agreement, the SWIFT MT103 receipt, the Formulario No. 5 filed by the bank, and the certificate issued by the Banco de la República.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments must be settled only after the corresponding Declaración de Cambio has been filed. For operational costs and trade payables: SWIFT MT103 via the local bank's correspondent network, accompanied by the declared purpose code. For payouts to agents and cash-pickup beneficiaries: the local bank routes funds through the national clearing system and regulated licensed agent network (Local_Cash_Pickup_Clearing), converting foreign currency to COP at the Tasa Representativa del Mercado (TRM). For international disbursements against commercial invoices: Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (Commercial LC) issued under UCP 600, with the S.A.S. as applicant and the foreign supplier as beneficiary; goods-related imports must be declared on Formulario No. 3. For all rails, the S.A.S. must maintain supporting documentation (invoice, contract, KYC-populated beneficiary list) and a sub-ledger reconciling SWIFT field 70/72 references. All foreign-currency settlements must pass through the mercado cambiario, and any unused FX position must be re-converted to COP within the statutory timeline.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable COP/USD foreign-exchange forwards executed with a locally authorized intermediario del mercado cambiario, backed by documented commercial or financial exposure.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on COP/USD arranged with offshore institutions on a hedging-need basis, settled in USD, and prohibited for speculative purposes.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) and single-currency interest-rate swaps used to align the S.A.S. funding currency with operational cash flows, subject to the Banco de la República's derivative-transaction requirements.
Vanilla FX options (puts or calls) purchased from a licensed bank for protection over committed foreign-currency flows, without leverage features.

FX forward repositioning permitted only against the registered foreign investment, trade receivables, or confirmed remittance-settlement pipeline; speculative use is prohibited under Resolución Externa No. 1 de 2018.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) — tariff reassessed based on total assets at the preceding December 31; USD amount is an estimate for a mid-market remittance SAS, the statutory tariff being asset-linked
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or the Cámara de Comercio of the registered corporate domicile)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each year; non-extendable closing date for the annual commercial renewal cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge (recargo por extemporaneidad) applied by the Chamber of Commerce; loss of good-standing certificates; two consecutive years of non-renewal cause classification as a non-operative company and lay the basis for administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings before the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders approving the prior-year financial statements, allocation of profits, and appointment or ratification of the Revisor Fiscal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (through deposit of the signed minutes and the approved financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year-end, that is, within three months after December 31, as required by Código de Comercio Article 190
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or hold the meeting blocks the legal payment of dividends; administrators become subject to inspection by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; the minutes will be rejected for Chamber registration if filed extemporaneously.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Statutory Financial Statements with the Commercial Registry (Depósito de Estados Financieros Certificados, with independent auditor's report if the Revisor Fiscal is mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the December 31 fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than March 31 of the following year, together with the shareholders' approval minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Chamber surcharges for the deferred deposit; impossibility of obtaining commercial registry certificates; persistent non-compliance triggers an order to regularize from the Superintendencia de Sociedades and may lead to forced liquidation of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 110 — Declaración de Renta y Complementario) for the immediately preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April of the year following the tax year, on the exact date assigned by the annual DIAN resolution based on the last two digits of the NIT (historically between April 8 and April 21)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneous filing surcharge under E.T. Article 642: 5% per month or fraction of the tax due, capped at 100% of the tax; monthly default interest runs on the unpaid balance; if omitted for 12 months or more, DIAN issues a proposed assessment on available evidentiary base.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Information Return (Información Exógena Tributaria) covering reportable payments, accruals, and cross-border remittance transaction annals of the prior tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, online portal only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June of the year following the tax year, on the tiered date fixed by the annual DIAN resolution by NIT last two digits (historically June 10 through June 26)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctions under E.T. Article 651: daily accrual of fines expressed in UVT up to a legal cap of 4,000 UVT (approximately USD 46,000 at the 2025 UVT); unpaid reportable amounts are flagged in DIAN cross-checks and lose evidentiary effect in support of deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update of the Ultimate Beneficial Owners Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales — Módulo BEF) under DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before September 30 of each year, reflecting the beneficial ownership situation as of the immediately preceding December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctions under the Tax Code as amended by Law 2155 of 2021: 100 UVT per day of delay without prejudice to the Chamber of Commerce refusing to issue good-standing certificates and to register director or share-transfer acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Regulatory Supervisory Information Package as required from licensed money-remittance services under Decreto 2555 of 2010
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the SFC reporting cycle: audited year-end financial statements and the corresponding regulatory annexes are due during the first quarter following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SFC administrative sanctions under the Financial Organization Statute, including fines up to 2,000 SMMLV and, for repeated or severe non-compliance, suspension of the money-transmission operating license or appointment of a delegated checker.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Colombian SAS must appoint a Revisor Fiscal (certified statutory auditor) when total gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (COP 7.118 billion for 2025, approximately USD 1.7 million), or gross annual income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approximately USD 1.0 million), or 200 or more employees are engaged. Because this scope covers a licensed money-transmission company supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, mandatory independent audit and Revisor Fiscal appointment apply irrespective of quantitative thresholds under Código de Comercio Article 207 and Decreto 2555 of 2010.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF Plenas (full IFRS) as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009 and implemented through Decree 2420 of 2015; the entity is classified as Group 1 for being an SFC-supervised financial-sector company, requiring IAS 1 presentation, IFRS 7 technical annexes, and the SFC's own disclosure formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2021 and the Chamber of Commerce beneficial-owner questionnaire, the SAS must identify and annually confirm its ultimate natural-person owners holding 10% or more of capital, control, or income rights. The BEF module confirmation is due every September 30. Intra-year share transfers must first be evidenced in the corporate books of share transfers; the updated UBO composition is then reflected in the March annual commercial renewal. A shareholder transfer recorded after the annual confirmation requires a corrected or amended report without waiting for the next September window, as non-current information triggers DIAN penalties and blocks further Chamber registrations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Minute Book for General Shareholders' Assemblies (Libro de Actas de Asamblea General de Accionistas)
Minute Book for Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva), when the SAS constitutes a board of directors
Supporting Ledger of Beneficial Owners and Share Transfers (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales y Cesiones)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% under Law 2277 of 2022 (Article 240 of the Colombian Tax Code / Estatuto Tributario), applicable to Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas (S.A.S.) as ordinary resident entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives:
No specific tax holiday applies to money-transmission or remittance activities. The effective rate may be lowered by: (i) a 25% income tax credit for qualified research, technological development and innovation investments (Article 256-1 ET); (ii) a 150% deductibility allowance for qualifying charitable donations; (iii) deductibility of the municipal ICA tax;
                (iv) inflationary adjustment mechanisms on financial costs and depreciation of the technology platform; and (v) inflation-adjusted depreciation on hardware serving the SWIFT and cash-pickup rails.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Cédula General de Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically through the DIAN 'Muisca' web portal by the legal representative using a digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, Form 110 must be filed between the first business days of September and mid-October of the immediately following year according to the schedule determined by the last two digits of the taxpayer NIT (for FY2024 return, the statutory window runs from approximately 8 August 2025 to 10 October 2025; large taxpayers and groups may have earlier deadlines).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of all gross ordinary income from fees, foreign exchange spreads, transaction commissions, correspondent banking credits and other operating revenues of the money-transmission business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All platform and remittance-linked revenues processed by the Colombian S.A.S. must be recognized; do not net against settlement costs. Foreign parent auditor reconciliation to the intercompany Form 1739 attachment is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and income not constituting taxable income or occasional gains, including capital contributions from the foreign shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only capital subscriptions actually paid into the S.A.S. are excluded; intercompany loans and SWIFT liquidity lines must be documented and treated as liabilities, and foreign exchange gains derived from the float must be taxed as ordinary income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating costs, deductions and amortizations: license fees for the SEDPE authorization, SARLAFT/AML compliance expenses, bank clearing and SWIFT fees, software platform maintenance, and employee payroll.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only invoices issued under Colombian e-invoicing rules and bearing a valid CUFE code are deductible. Costs paid to foreign group IT vendors are deductible only if supported by the TP documentation and a threshold beneficial-ownership analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses of the current period and prior-year tax losses that are compensated against the current taxable base (five-year carryforward under Law 2277 of 2022).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss must arise from the Colombian taxable activity; a foreign parent cannot force a Colombian loss through excessive intercompany fees. The loss trail must be evidenced in the annual transfer pricing report and the tax loss calculation annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net liquid taxable income: gross income minus non-taxable income, costs, deductions, and losses actually compensated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. must ensure the resulting base remains positive and realistic relative to its licensed activities. A negative base artificially created by intra-group interest payments to the foreign parent will be disregarded and re-characterized as a constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the income tax charge at the 35% statutory rate over the net liquid taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full 35% is imposed at entity level; remittance fees are not subject to any special bank surcharge because the S.A.S. is not a bank or credit institution for purposes of Article 239 ET.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable before credits and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must equal the sum of all monthly withholding statements filed as a withholding agent; material discrepancies between Form 110 and Form 100 monthly withholding returns trigger automatic DIAN cross-checks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax discounts: 25% R&D&I credit and any other legally authorized discount, deductible assistance mechanisms, and double taxation credits derived from treaty and domestic source rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The R&D credit must be supported by a valid Colombian research contract and certification with the Ministry of Science. Foreign headquarters R&D does not qualify unless re-issued to the Colombian entity with a Colombian substantive lab.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance to pay or balance in favor (saldo a pagar or saldo a favor) after deducting withholdings, installments, advances and tax discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If balance in favor is claimed, the foreign parent must expect a mandatory 'crosschecking' review of the entire Form 110 and attachment data; excess balances are rarely paid to non-resident shareholders and must be utilized against future liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic signing by the legal representative and by a certified public accountant (Contador Público) where the gross income level so requires.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The legal representative must be physically present and economically connected to the Colombian business; a resident nominee without authority over the bank account and payment rails invalidates the filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty accrues at 5% of the income tax payable for each month or fraction of delay, up to a 100% ceiling of the tax declared; after 12 months, the penalty is increased to a fixed 10% of the liability plus daily moratory interest at the DIAN variable rate (approximately 20%–25% per annum in 2025). Failure to file at all leads to an official assessment based on net worth tests and the allowed gross income, and interest is charged from the original due date without offset.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1739 – Información de Vinculados / Transfer Pricing Declaration; filed through the DIAN 'Muisca' portal by the same electronic signature, on an annual basis.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due no later than the same general deadline as Form 110 for the corresponding fiscal year, based on the NIT-digit DIAN calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification of each related foreign or resident counterparty, including the foreign parent, the SWIFT clearing agent and any affiliated software or cash-pickup enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The exact legal name, country of residence and identifiable foreign tax number of each cross-border counterparty must be stated; a beneficial ownership declaration (Form W-BEN equivalent) and an electronic TRC from the counterpart's tax authority must be attached for each related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DIAN codification of the type of operation performed: loans, services, royalties, technology licensing, commission sharing, or operational leasing of the remittance rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mischaracterizing a royalty as a service or a loan as a cash float is a recurring audit trigger. Remittance fees shared with foreign network correspondents must be classified as service transactions and matched with the contractual agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The arm's-length method selected for the transaction described.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent guidance: for the remittance agency fee to the Colombian entity, TNMM with the operating margin over operating costs is typical; for the SWIFT correspondent clearing commissions, CUP may be used; any profit-split method on float revenues requires the full demonstration of global integration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Value charged, accrued or settled during the tax period for each transaction, expressed in COP with the foreign currency conversion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the official DIAN exchange rate average for translation; unrealized foreign-currency differences must be reported consistently between Form 110 and Form 1739 and the foreign parent's supporting financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the comparable data, internal or external, and quantitative adjustments applied (working capital, risk, functions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian entity should source comparables tested against the local market for payment-correspondent agency operations; a statement signed by the foreign parent's tax director is expected for each selected benchmark.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loans, liquidity lines and interest paid to the foreign parent or affiliated treasury; includes the average balance, interest rate, maturity and the withholding position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Debt from the foreign parent exceeding the 3:1 thin capitalization cap will produce non-deductible interest; a comprehensive loan agreement with payment flows through the SWIFT rail, market-rate interest and repayment evidence must be filed with the TP return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 1739 or filing with inaccurate, incomplete or absent comparables subjects the S.A.S. to sanctions under Articles 651 and 260-11 ET, generally between COP 17 million and COP 119 million (2025 UVT-based), and permits the DIAN to make an official re-pricing of the transactions using a standard margin without accepting taxpayer comparables; such adjustments generate additional assessed income taxed at 35% plus moratory interest and a 100%-plus inflationary sanction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid to a non-resident legal or individual shareholder when the dividend is distributed from income already subject to Colombian CIT (Article 245 ET, amended by Law 2010 of 2019); distributions made out of strictly non-taxed income attract the 35% general rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal / TRC) issued by its own tax authority for the relevant calendar year; submission is made through the DIAN Muisca service 'Solicitud de Aplicación de Convenio para Evitar la Doble Tributación' together with the payer's beneficial-owner declaration and, where applicable, a certificate of effective activity demonstrating that the recipient is not a conduit; the Colombian payer must preserve the entire file for the six-year audit window, and the reduced treaty rate applies only upon a formal DIAN acknowledgment or a reasoned internal analysis prior to the payment date; in the absence of treaty or non-compliance, the 10% statutory rate is withheld and no refund exists for the fail-fast procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for software, technology or trademarks paid to a foreign beneficiary: statutory withholding rate 15% under Article 408 ET; treaty relief commonly lowers this to 10% or 15% under the relevant DTA. Interest paid to non-resident financial or related-party lenders: statutory 15% under Articles 402–403 ET; the withholding increase to 35% applies when the lender is located in a tax-haven jurisdiction or where the interest beneficiary lacks the relevant financial intermediation substance; treaty rates on interest generally range from 10% to 15% depending on the specific bilateral agreement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Form 1739 filing applies when the Colombian entity's consolidated gross income exceeds COP 4,232,915,000 (85,000 UVTs of 2025 at COP 49,799 per UVT, per Law 2277 of 2022 reducing the former 100,000-UVT threshold); Master File is compulsory when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds 450,000 UVTs (approximately COP 22.4 billion) and in all cases where the foreign parent aggregates operations above DIAN Resolution 126 of 2023 annex thresholds; even below the filing threshold, contemporaneous documentation is required as soon as any cross-border intercompany transaction occurs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime of the offshore type, but the combination of Law 2277 of 2022's General Anti-Abuse Rule, the CFC rules, the DTA beneficial-ownership tests and the DIAN's substance-over-form doctrine impose an effective economic substance requirement. A remittance S.A.S. must prove local management, an operational office in Colombia, legal title and control over its payment-rail contracts, substantive local staff, active bank accounts and business purpose; a mere nominal SAS owning the revenue stream while all functions are exercised abroad by the non-resident parent is vulnerable to being re-characterized as a conduit, losing treaty eligibility and attracting the full 35% rate on all remitted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Income Tax Evasion and False Invoice Trafficking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring gross remittance commissions and foreign-exchange spreads; deducting invoices issued by shell suppliers or 'factureras' for fake technology, marketing or operational services, thereby reducing the Colombian corporate income tax base with non-genuine costs; hiding the controlling ultimate beneficial owner through bearer-like nominee structures to obstruct the DIAN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 100% of the tax understated (160% where the evasion involves documents falsified to mislead the tax administration), moratory interest at the variable DIAN annual rate, business closure for up to 10 days for failure to exhibit accounting books, and criminal conviction under Article 434B of the Criminal Code carrying imprisonment from 48 to 108 months and fines from COP 200 million to COP 1,200 million; the criminal consequence applies at the legal representative and responsible officer level.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under Article 42 of the Commercial Code when the S.A.S. is used as a mere facade: directors, shareholders and the de facto officer are personally, severally and jointly liable for all unpaid taxes, penalties and interest, with civil restitution orders over personal property, restrictive travel bans preventing the directors from leaving Colombia, and imprisonment for the officers who signed or ordered the false declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mismatch and Missing Transfer Pricing Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 1739 or the Local File; applying an over-aggressive foreign exchange spread against the SWIFT correspondents without comparables; assigning all residual profit to the non-resident parent while leaving the Colombian entity with a zero or negative margin; ignoring the thin-capitalization cap on intercompany debt used to finance the remittance rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Official DIAN re-determination of the taxable base at arm's length plus a 20% penalty on the adjusted tax liability and the additional tax at 35% plus moratory interest; the TP documentation penalties under Article 260-11 ET amount to between approximately COP 17 million and COP 119 million per return (Form 1739) and up to 10% of the intercompany transaction value when the information is omitted or incorrect; failure to produce contemporaneous documentation reverses the burden of proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the Form 1739 with deliberately manipulated comparables or who direct the transfer of float income abroad are jointly liable for the re-assessed tax, may be subject to a personal restitution order for the shifted profit, encounter restrictions on the conversion of personal assets to cash, and can be criminally indicted for tax fraud where the adjustment exceeds the criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Unlicensed Money Transmission Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cross-border remittance service without the mandatory SEDPE license required by Law 1735 of 2014 (sociedad especializada en depósitos y pagos), making cash-pickup pay-outs through unregistered FIU agents, or failing to build the SARLAFT/AML internal control system with the transaction-threshold reporting (UBRO) and the direct registration of the beneficial shareholder before the UIAF; facilitating onward settlement of funds for expatriate workers through unlicensed parallel riders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to COP 1,500,000,000 imposed by the Financial Superintendence (SFC), revocation of any auxiliary payment-rail authorization and negative registration in the UIAF risk list; the unauthorized intermediation of payment transactions is criminally sanctioned under Article 106 of the Organic Financial Statute with imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and fines up to COP 5,000,000,000; laundering of the settlement float or of third-party criminally sourced proceeds triggers Criminal Code Article 323 with imprisonment of 10 to 30 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and the compliance officer who knowingly operate without a license or who tolerate AML breaches are subject to exclusion orders prohibiting any financial-sector activity for up to 20 years, personal civil restitution for the funds moved illicitly, seizure of the personal shareholdings of the foreign shareholder, and criminal incarceration; the corporate veil is expressly lifted for illicit assets under the money-laundering forfeiture regime with the burden on the S.A.S. to prove legitimate origin of every asset.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Conduit Abuse and Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the Colombian S.A.S. as a zero-substance conduit: no operating employees in Bogotá, no independent control of bank accounts, no local IT equipment, no physical office, all decision-making with the foreign parent, and routing of remittance revenues through a sham Colombian entity solely to access treaty protection or to defer the 10% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty dividend, interest and royalty rate relief under the beneficial-owner and limitation-on-benefits provisions of the Colombia DTA network; recharacterization of all distributed funds as constructive dividends taxed at 10% or 35% as applicable, plus losses of all cost deductions attributable to the conduit arrangements; the anti-abuse rule in Law 2277 imposes an additional fine of up to 100%–300% of the underpaid withholding tax and a requirement to adjust the domestic tax base against the hidden profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foreign beneficial owner and the local nominee director face joint and several personal liability for the full withholding difference, the unpaid taxes and treble penalties; the nominee director is barred from serving as legal representative for a period of 10 years, personal travel bans are available where enforcement actions remain unsatisfied, and in aggravated cross-border cases the public prosecutor proceeds for document fraud and money-laundering with applicable prison terms of 4.5 to 15 years.
